hints: Positions are one-indexed, so the first digit is at k=1.
Count the digits contributed by all numbers with 1 digit, then 2 digits, and so on until k falls inside a block.
Within that block, divide the offset by the digit width to find the number, then use the remainder to select its digit.
analogy: Skip whole pages of equal-width numbers, then locate one digit on the page where the position lands.
example: At k=12, digits 1..9 use 9 places; offset 3 in the two-digit block is number 11's second digit, namely 1.
algorithm: For digit width d, the block has 9*10^(d-1)*d digits. Subtract full blocks; derive number=10^(d-1)+(k-1)/d and digit index=(k-1)%d.
correctness: The blocks partition the infinite string by number length; quotient selects the number and remainder selects its exact character.
complexity: O(log k) time and O(1) extra space using a wide integer type.
